cards.text: Hosea is a prophet, and the word of the LORD came to him (Hos 1:1). This message is for the people of Israel, and it opens by shutting a celebration down: 'Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations…'

cards.question: Hosea tells Israel not to celebrate like the nations do. Why not?

answers.text: They've been unfaithful to their God
They just lost their king in battle
Their harvest came in far too late

cards.text: Hosea calls it playing the harlot against God, making 'love for hire on every threshing floor.' Keep your eye on those threshing floors, friend, because Hosea's not done with them.

cards.question: True or false: The threshing floor and the winepress will keep feeding Israel.

cards.text: Then it gets heavier: they won't remain in the land of the LORD, and Ephraim, another name Hosea uses for Israel (Hos 11:8), will return to Egypt. Yes, EGYPT, the very place God called His son Israel out of (Hos 11:1).

cards.question: Ephraim is headed back to Egypt. Where else will they end up eating unclean food?

cards.text: Out there, no wine offerings to the LORD, and no sacrifices that please Him. Hosea says they'll be 'like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled,' and friend, nobody wants to be part of a batch like that.

cards.question: True or false: Hosea says Israel's bread will still go into the house of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Hosea asks, 'What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?' Picture the biggest baking day of the year, and you're stuck across town with no oven, just standing there holding a bag of chocolate chips.

cards.question: Hosea says even if Israel flees destruction, Egypt will gather them. Which city will bury them?
True or false: Hosea pictures Israel's tents overrun with thorns.

cards.text: Now the alarm sounds: 'The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived…' Hosea says let Israel know it, and friend, there's no snooze button on this one.

cards.question: God's prophet is warning Israel, and the prophet gets called a ___.

cards.text: And Hosea says why: because Israel's iniquity and hostility are so great. That's like yelling 'The OVEN'S SMOKING!' and the whole kitchen says, 'Somebody check on Dorin, he's lost it.'
Hosea calls the prophet Ephraim's watchman, along with Hosea's God, and then adds, 'Hostility is in the house of his God!' Not out in the street, friend, right there in the HOUSE of God.

cards.question: Ephraim's watchman is on the job. What lies on all his paths?

answers.text: A trap set to catch him

cards.text: Hosea says they have 'deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah…' Gibeah is a town in Benjamin (Josh 18:28), and Hosea doesn't spell out what happened there, but it's nothing good.

cards.question: Hosea says God will remember Israel's ___ and punish their sins.

cards.text: Now the LORD speaks: 'I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.' That's like finding a warm cookie in the back of a junk drawer, and believe me, friend, I'd REMEMBER that.
He saw their fathers as the first figs of the season. But they went to Baal-peor, where Israel joined in worshiping Baal back in Numbers 25, and 'consecrated themselves to Shame…'

cards.question: Israel's fathers gave themselves to Shame at Baal-peor. What did they become?

answers.text: As detestable as what they loved
As strong as the nations around them
As free as birds in the wilderness

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird…' Friend, I've watched birds leave a windowsill, and they do NOT come back to say goodbye.

cards.question: Ephraim's glory flies away like a bird. What will Ephraim have none of?

cards.text: Even if they raise children, the LORD says He will bereave them of each one. That's a heavy line, friend, and Hosea doesn't soften it.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says woe to Ephraim when He turns away from them.

cards.text: The LORD says He has seen Ephraim like Tyre, planted in a meadow. Tyre was a rich trading city on the sea (Ezek 27:33).

cards.question: True or false: Ephraim, planted like Tyre in a meadow, will bring out his children for slaughter.

cards.text: Then the prophet turns to the LORD and asks what He will give them. I think you can hear him stopping to find the words.

cards.question: The prophet asks what the LORD will give Ephraim. What does he land on?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks again: 'All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them.' Hosea already said not to go to Gilgal (Hos 4:15).

cards.question: Because of their wicked deeds, where will the LORD drive Ephraim from?

cards.text: I think this is the hardest line in the whole passage: 'I will no longer love them…' Read that one slow, friend.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says all of Ephraim's leaders are rebellious.

cards.text: Remember the grapes and the first figs? Now the picture is a plant in the ground, and it's in trouble: 'Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered…'

cards.question: Ephraim is like a plant with a withered root. Hosea says they cannot bear ___.
True or false: The LORD says that even if Ephraim bears children, those children will be spared.

cards.text: Then the prophet sums it all up in one plain line: 'My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him…'

cards.question: Rejected by God, what will Israel become among the nations?
